rv.q: IT'S BEEN TEN YEARS SINCE EVERYBODY DIED, misses the mark on both scares and astute social commentary, but through no fault of its talented and refreshingly diverse cast.
If some of Ortiz's plot points ultimately don't land as they should, just as Talo's direction sometimes lacks the needed rhythmic punch, this is still an original, noteworthy work.

Cesario Tirado-Ortiz is a playwright, actor, singer, producer (and, no doubt, pastry chef and bricklayer!), and it’s been ten years follows his tradition of telling queer stories that are not necessarily about being queer.
But Tirado-Ortiz's story... shows a playwright with promise and moxie.
I left this show shaking my head. I was confused, let down and dissatisfied with what I had just experienced.
This show is a unique experience and you will be talking about it long after the actors take their bow.

The Final Survivors Support Group Hosted at Open Space Arts Our story starts with former friends leading their different lives ten years after traumatic events changed their lives forever. Allison (Noah Hinton) the awkward trans girl. Maude (Julia Toney) the loner that challenges authority and is ready to fight against anything.
